;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Darfur]]
**Nine people were killed and twenty others injured during a [[shooting]] on a camp for internally displaced people in [[Kutum]], [[Sudan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/condemns-deadly-violence-sudan-north-darfur-200715094909361.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020 Armenian–Azerbaijani skirmishes]]; [[Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]
**[[Armenia]]n and [[Azerbaijan]]i forces exchange fire on the [[Armenia–Azerbaijan border|border]], leaving three [[Azerbaijani Land Forces|Azeri soldiers]] dead and five wounded, according to Azerbaijan's [[Ministry of Defence (Azerbaijan)|Ministry of Defence]]. No [[Armenian Army|Armenian]] casualties are reported. [https://eurasiantimes.com/azerbaijan-armenia-border-clash-azerbaijani-soldiers-killed-in-border-clash-with-armenia/ (''The Eurasian Times'')] [https://en.armradio.am/2020/07/12/azerbaijan-reports-third-death/ (Armenia Radio)]

;Business and economy
*The [[McClatchy|McClatchy company]],  one of the largest and most respected American news publishers, announces that hedge fund Chatham Asset Management won its bankruptcy sale in a court-supervised auction. Chatham, which owns the ''[[National Enquirer]]'', has been an investor in the company since 2009. Court confirmation, likely at a hearing on July 24, is required.  McClatchy has been burdened by heavy debt  from its large pension obligations and the acquisition of newspaper chain [[Knight Ridder]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mcclatchy-bankruptcy-chatham-asset-ma/hedge-fund-chathams-bid-wins-auction-for-miami-herald-publisher-mcclatchy-idUSKCN24D0ND (Reuters)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/12/business/media/hedge-fund-mcclatchy-newspapers.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*A fire, followed by an explosion, breaks out on the [[USS Bonhomme Richard (LHD-6)|USS ''Bonhomme Richard'']] at the [[Naval Base San Diego|U.S. Naval base in San Diego]], California. At least 18 sailors are currently hospitalized. It is unclear where the fire started or what the source of the explosion was. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/12/us/naval-ship-fire-san-diego.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://thehill.com/policy/defense/506971-firefighters-respond-to-blaze-on-board-us-navy-ship (''The Hill'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]], [[Japan–United States relations]]
***[[U.S. military]] officials report 61 cases of COVID-19 at [[Marine Corps Air Station Futenma]] and [[Camp Hansen]]. Governor of [[Okinawa Prefecture]] [[Denny Tamaki]] said late on Saturday that "Okinawans are shocked by what we were told", and demanded more action from the U.S. military which has since put the two bases under lockdown. [https://apnews.com/6ab5fdce20c475111cbc65409851692c (AP News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****[[Florida]] reports 15,299 cases, a new single-day record. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/jul/12/15000-new-coronavirus-cases-florida-record-daily-total-us (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
***The death toll in [[Mexico]] rises above 35,000, surpassing [[Italy]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-mexico-idUSKCN24D0NP (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*Aftermath of the [[Sudanese Revolution]]
**Amid a series of reforms, [[government of Sudan|Sudan]] bans [[female genital mutilation]], decriminalizes [[apostasy]], ends public flogging and lifts a 36-year ban on the consumption of [[Alcohol (drug)|alcohol]] for non-[[Islam in Sudan|Muslims]], according to Justice Minister [[Nasreldin Abdelbari]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53379733 (BBC News)]
*China releases law professor [[Xu Zhangrun]], who had criticized [[General Secretary of the Communist Party of China|CCP General Secretary]] [[Xi Jinping]] and the [[Communist Party of China|Chinese Communist Party]] (CCP), from detention after six days. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-politics-professor/china-releases-professor-who-criticised-president-xi-friends-say-idUSKCN24D0AW (Reuters)]
*Police in Boston and in New York are investigating attacks on statues of the Virgin Mary at local Catholic churches. In [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston|Boston]], a statue outside St. Peter’s Church in [[Dorchester, Boston|Dorchester]] neighborhood was set on fire, causing serious damage. In [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Brooklyn|New York]], an unidentified man was shown on security videotape painting the word “idol” on a statue outside [[Cathedral Preparatory School and Seminary|Cathedral Prep School]] in [[Queens]]. [https://www.catholicworldreport.com/2020/07/12/statues-of-mary-vandalized-in-weekend-of-church-attacks/ (Catholic News Agency)]

;Politics and elections

**The second round of the latest [[Elections in Poland|presidential election]] in [[Poland]] takes place. Incumbent [[President of Poland|President]] [[Andrzej Duda]] faces [[Mayor of Warsaw]] [[Rafał Trzaskowski]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/12/poland-presidential-election-too-close-to-call-voting-begins-andrzej-duda-rafa-trzaskowski (''The Guardian'')]
